key_insight: Annealing a tailored Ni-based sprayed coating at 800°C for 1 h produced a refined three-phase microstructure and reduced wear rate by 89%.
engineering_relevance: Controlled crystallization offers a route to wear-resistant coatings that combine hard load-bearing phases with a ductile, crack-resistant matrix.
method: Thermally spray amorphous Ni68.6Cr8.7Nb3P16B3.2Si0.5 alloy powder.
Anneal at 800°C for 1 h to transform the metastable phase into Ni-based solid solution, Ni3P, and NbNi3.
Evaluate microstructure, friction, wear rate, and worn-surface damage.
evidence_signal: Relative to the as-sprayed coating, annealing reduced intersplat density by 51%, coefficient of friction by 21%, and wear rate by 89%, with no observed worn-surface cracking, delamination, or spallation.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify wear-test conditions or substrate compatibility with the 800°C anneal, limiting assessment of service applicability.
paper_title: Enhanced Wear Resistance of Fine-Grained Ni-Based Coating via Annealing-Induced Phase Transformation
